memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Neither," he replied, "but as commander of the army of the Lord I have now come." Then Joshua fell facedown to the ground in reverence, and asked him, "What message does my Lord have for his servant?" — Josh 5:14 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The answer is unexpected: "Neither." This heavenly commander does not slot neatly onto Joshua's side or the enemy's side. He comes as the commander of the Lord's own army, and the real question is whether Joshua will fall in line under Him. And Joshua does exactly that — he falls facedown in reverence and asks, "What message does my Lord have for his servant?"

Watch the beautiful shift in Joshua. He came asking, "Are you for us?" as though he were in charge, sizing up an ally. Now he lies on the ground calling himself a servant, ready to receive orders. That is the posture of true faith: not directing God, but bowing before Him and asking, "What would You have me do?"

This is where real strength for the battle is found — not in Joshua's military planning, but in his surrender to the true Commander. Jericho would not be conquered by Joshua's strategy but by Joshua's obedience to the Lord who was already at work.

Many understand this "commander of the army of the Lord," whom Joshua worships without rebuke, to be a special appearance of the pre-incarnate Son of God, for a mere angel would refuse worship (Rev 22:8-9). Whether or not we can be certain of that, the response God calls for is clear. Before the risen Christ, the true Commander of heaven's armies, we too are called to bow and say, "What would You have me do?" (Acts 9:6). Victory begins on our faces before Him.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Is your posture before God more like giving orders or receiving them?
2. What would it look like to fall facedown and ask, "What message do You have for Your servant?"
3. Where do you need to surrender your strategy and simply obey the true Commander?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, I bow before You as Your servant. Not my strategy, but Your command; not my will, but Yours. Speak, and help me obey. Amen.
